messages:
Alex: Morning — quick async check for the content calendar + benchmark notes.
What I did yesterday: scheduled two posts (product roundup + launch tips), ran a baseline perf bench on the marketing blog experiment (image lazy-loading).
Blockers: waiting on final SEO copy from @Maria and the hero image crop from @Noah.
Today: will push final copy to staging, confirm publish windows, and re-run the bench after the image update.

Maria: On it — I’ll review the SEO copy by 11:30am PT and leave inline comments in Notion. Link: https://notion.redwood/content/launch-tips

Sam: Quick bench note — after the initial loader change CPU p95 is ~180ms, p99 ~320ms on staging with current images. I pushed a small tweak to the loader; can someone smoke-test the public endpoint? `curl -I https://staging.redwood.com/launch`

Jin: FYI — cache state matters for those numbers. For consistent comparisons use a cold-cache tag: `?cache=cold`. Also suggest running 3 sequential runs and taking median p95.

Noah: I can do the image crops in ~30m and upload to Figma. If Maria is blocked I can also swap in a temporary hero so publishing isn’t delayed.

ContentBot: Scheduled post IDs: 1287, 1288. ETA publish window: 08:00-09:00 UTC on Wed. :white_check_mark:

Alex: Thanks — @Maria if you give approval I’ll flip the scheduled flag and ping #launch-ops to start the deploy smoke tests. If anyone sees SEO regressions after staging push, paste examples here.

Maria: Header typo fixed, approved. :thumbsup:

Sam: Smoke-tested the endpoint after loader tweak and new images — p95 down to ~150ms, p99 ~310ms. :tada:

Jin: Ran three cold-cache runs, results below:
```
run1: p95 152ms p99 315ms
run2: p95 148ms p99 322ms
run3: p95 150ms p99 318ms
```

Alex: Great — flipping the scheduled flag now and will drop a short update in #launch-ops once live. Thanks all!
